title: Reproduction in Plants and Animals
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Reproduction in Plants and Animals Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the form and function of reproductive cells and organs in animals and plants, and analyse how the processes of sexual and asexual reproduction enable survival of the species (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on reproduction: sexual and asexual reproduction, gametes, human reproductive organs, fertilisation and development, flowers, pollination and seeds. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents; asexual reproduction copies one parent.
body_html:
How to think about it

Reproduction makes new individuals so a species survives.

  • Sexual reproduction: a male and a female gamete join (fertilisation). Offspring vary, which helps when conditions change.
  • Asexual reproduction: one parent, no gametes (runners, cuttings, budding). Fast, but offspring are identical clones.
  • Flowers: anthers make pollen, the stigma catches it, and the ovule in the ovary becomes a seed after fertilisation.
Example

Strawberry runner: sexual or asexual?

one parent

clone

Answer: asexual

Example

Where is the egg fertilised?

egg leaves the ovary

meets sperm in the oviduct

Answer: the oviduct

Common mistakes

  • Thinking sexual reproduction needs only one parent.
  • Mixing up the ovary (makes eggs) and the uterus (where the baby grows).
  • Thinking offspring from asexual reproduction are all different.

faq.q: Why do many species use both kinds of reproduction?
faq.a: Asexual reproduction is fast when conditions are good. Sexual reproduction creates variation that helps the species survive when conditions change.

faq.q: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
faq.a: Pollination is pollen landing on the stigma. Fertilisation happens later, when the male gamete from the pollen joins the egg in the ovule.

faq.q: How are marsupials different from placental mammals?
faq.a: Marsupials, such as kangaroos, give birth to tiny young that grow in a pouch. Placental mammals grow inside the uterus with a placenta until they are more developed.

items.q: What is one advantage of sexual reproduction?
c: Variation helps some offspring survive if the environment changes.
items.e: Variation is useful.

items.q: Ethan reads: “A hydra grows a bud that breaks off.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be identical to the parent's.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: Mia reads: “Two dogs have a litter of puppies.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: Why are offspring from sexual reproduction different from each other?
c: They get a different mix of genes from each parent.
items.e: Variation helps a species survive change.

items.q: Mia reads: “Bees carry pollen so flowers make seeds.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be identical to one parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: A red kangaroo joey is born tiny and grows in its mother's pouch. What kind of mammal is a kangaroo?
items.e: Marsupials carry young in a pouch.

items.q: What is the main difference between sexual and asexual reproduction?
c: Sexual reproduction joins two gametes from two parents; asexual reproduction needs only one parent.
items.e: Sexual offspring vary; asexual offspring are clones.

items.q: How many sets of chromosomes does a human get from each parent?
c: one set (23 chromosomes) from each parent

items.q: Mia reads: “A hydra grows a bud that breaks off.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: Why are offspring from asexual reproduction identical to the parent?
c: They get half from each of two parents.
They receive a copy of all of one parent's genetic information.
items.e: One parent, copied DNA.

items.q: Why do offspring from sexual reproduction show variation?
c: They get half their chromosomes from each parent, in new combinations.
They are copies of one parent.
items.e: Mixing creates variation.

items.q: What is one advantage of asexual reproduction?
c: One parent can make many offspring quickly.
items.e: Fast and simple.

items.q: Each year, corals on the Great Barrier Reef release eggs and sperm into the water on the same nights. Why?
items.e: Mass spawning puts many gametes together.

items.q: Kai reads: “Two dogs have a litter of puppies.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be identical to one parent's.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: Lachlan reads: “A bacterium splits into two cells.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be identical to the parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: Many wattle seeds only sprout after a bushfire. How does this help the species survive?
c: Seeds grow when there is space, light and nutrients after the fire.
items.e: Many Australian plants are adapted to fire.

items.q: What are the male and female gametes in humans?
items.e: Gametes are sex cells.

items.q: Ruby reads: “A strawberry plant sends out runners that grow new plants.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be identical to the parent's.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of asexual reproduction?
c: All offspring are identical, so one disease can kill them all.
items.e: Banana plantations are at risk for this reason.

items.q: Priya reads: “Bees carry pollen so flowers make seeds.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: What does 'puberty' mean?
c: the organ that links the foetus's blood supply to the mother's
the time from fertilisation to birth
the time when the body changes and the reproductive organs start to work
the release of an egg from an ovary
items.e: Learn the key words.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system is the bag of skin that holds the testes?
items.e: Each part of the reproductive system has a job.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system is a ring of muscle at the opening of the uterus?

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system carries sperm from the testes towards the penis?

items.q: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?

items.e: Strawberry runners spread quickly.

items.q: Which word means the time when the body changes and the reproductive organs start to work?

items.q: In a 28-day cycle, during which days is fertilisation most likely?
items.e: Sperm can survive a few days and the egg about a day around ovulation.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system carries semen or urine out through the penis?
items.e: The urethra in the male: carries semen or urine out through the penis.

items.q: In a regular 28-day menstrual cycle that starts on day 1, on about which day is an egg released (ovulation)?
items.e: Ovulation usually happens about halfway through the cycle.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system makes sperm cells?
items.e: Each part of the reproductive system has a job.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system is where the foetus develops?
items.e: The uterus (womb): is where the foetus develops.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system carries the egg from the ovary to the uterus, and is where fertilisation happens?
items.e: Each part of the reproductive system has a job.

items.q: Menstruation in a 28-day cycle lasts from day 1 to day 5. What is happening?
c: The thickened lining of the uterus breaks down and is lost with some blood.
items.e: This happens when the egg is not fertilised.

items.q: Where does fertilisation usually happen in humans?
items.e: The fertilised egg then moves to the uterus.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system receives sperm during sexual intercourse and is the birth canal?
items.e: The vagina: receives sperm during sexual intercourse and is the birth canal.

items.q: A girl's period started on 8 March. She has a regular 28-day cycle. When is her next period likely to start?
items.e: Add 28 days to the first day of the period.

items.q: Which word means the time from fertilisation to birth?
items.e: Learn the key words.

when the embryo attaches to the lining of the uterus
a developing baby once its organs have formed
the release of an egg from an ovary
items.e: Learn the key words.

items.q: Which word means the release of an egg from an ovary?
items.e: Learn the key words.

items.q: Which part of the reproductive system contains eggs and release one about once a month?
items.e: Each part of the reproductive system has a job.

the egg travels along the oviduct

items.q: What are the male and female gametes in a flowering plant?

items.q: Lachlan reads: “Some cattle breeds naturally grow more muscle than others.” Is the difference mainly caused by an environmental factor or a genetic factor?

items.e: Genes set the possible range; the environment affects where in that range an organism grows.

items.q: Ruby studies a plant structure: corn plants with feathery tassels. What does this structure mainly help with?
items.e: Pollination moves pollen; dispersal moves seeds.

items.q: Liam wants to test which way of dispersing seeds travels furthest. Which fair test could he use?
c: drop different seeds from the same height in front of the same fan and measure the distance
use different fans for each seed
items.e: Keep everything the same except the seed.

items.q: Jack counts pollen grains that germinate in sugar solutions of 0%, 5%, 10% and 15%. What is the independent variable?
items.e: He changes the sugar concentration.

items.q: Why do bees matter to farmers who grow apples and strawberries?
c: Bees pollinate the flowers, so fruits form.
items.e: Pollinators.

items.q: Priya reads: “Corn grown in a drought is much shorter than the same corn with enough water.” Is the difference mainly caused by an environmental factor or a genetic factor?
c: the season of the year only
items.e: Genes set the possible range; the environment affects where in that range an organism grows.

items.q: Amelia covers some flowers on a tomato plant with paper bags so insects cannot reach them. What is she testing?
c: whether insects are needed for pollination and fruit
items.e: Compare covered and uncovered flowers.

items.q: Noah measures the length of a human embryo and foetus: 1 cm at 8 weeks, 6 cm at 12 weeks and 16 cm at 20 weeks. What does the data show?
c: It grows faster as the pregnancy goes on.
It grows the same amount each week.
items.e: Growth speeds up after the organs form.

items.q: Some aphids reproduce asexually in summer and sexually in autumn. What is a likely benefit?
c: Fast growth in good times and variation before harsh conditions.
items.e: Both strategies have advantages.

items.q: Why does a mother need a healthy diet during pregnancy?
c: The placenta makes food from nothing.
The foetus gets its nutrients from her blood through the placenta.
items.e: Healthy lifestyle.

items.q: Ella says a banana plantation of clones is at risk from a new fungus. Why?
c: All plants have the same genes, so none may resist it.
items.e: Lack of variation is risky.

items.q: Zara grows yeast in warm sugar water and sees buds forming on cells. What kind of reproduction is this?
items.e: Each bud becomes a new cell.

items.q: Self-pollination uses pollen from the same plant. What is one disadvantage?
items.e: Cross-pollination increases variation.

items.q: Why is an egg cell much bigger than a sperm cell?
c: It contains a food store for the embryo.
items.e: Food for the early embryo.

items.q: Why does a sperm cell have a tail?
items.e: Adapted for its job.

items.q: Jack reads: “Fish in a crowded pond grow smaller than the same kind of fish in a large lake.” Is the difference mainly caused by an environmental factor or a genetic factor?
c: the season of the year only
items.e: Genes set the possible range; the environment affects where in that range an organism grows.

items.q: Ruby compares bean seeds germinating at 5 °C, 15 °C and 25 °C. Most sprout at 25 °C. What can she conclude?
c: Warmth (up to 25 °C) helps bean seeds germinate.
Cold is best for all seeds.
items.e: Repeat with more seeds to check.

items.q: What happens to the lining of the uterus if an egg is not fertilised?
c: It breaks down and leaves the body as a period.
items.e: The menstrual cycle.

items.q: Ruby's banana plants are all clones grown from cuttings. A new disease appears. Why is this risky?
c: They are genetically identical, so if one is vulnerable, all are.
items.e: No variation means no resistant plants.

items.q: Why is seed dispersal important?
c: It reduces competition with the parent plant for light, water and nutrients.
It helps the parent grow taller.
items.e: Less competition.

items.q: Chloe reads: “A plant from tall parent plants grows tall in good conditions.” Is the difference mainly caused by an environmental factor or a genetic factor?
c: the season of the year only
items.e: Genes set the possible range; the environment affects where in that range an organism grows.

items.q: Why are the results of a seed-falling test repeated and averaged?
c: to make the results more reliable
because the first result is always wrong
items.e: Repeat readings.
